title: Tales of Genetics: African Giants
summary: Story time about the genetic freaks of African origin he has met: a 7-foot-plus giant in his neighborhood in France, the ever-present huge man benching 500 lb in every gym, and a first-timer who overhead pressed 225 for five reps. His point is that genetics really matter and these people start at a level others can never reach.
claims: In every gym he joined there was one enormous man, always Black in his experience, around 300 lb, benching 500 lb for reps with no spotter while paying no attention to volume or intensity
These gym giants tend to be the nicest guys; they just come in, bench and go home without peaking or programming
At 6 ft he is tall for France, yet he once walked next to a man of about 7 ft 2 whose head he could not see under his umbrella
A roughly 6 ft 8 man on his first day ever in a gym overhead pressed 225 lb for 5 reps with no training
Legends of people deadlifting 400 lb the first time they touch a weight are real; that cannot be taught, you are born with it
Such genetically gifted people become champions because their starting level is so high that once they progress no one can compete
He states he will never overhead press 225 lb in his life
Genetics do matter, but it does not matter for you because you cannot change yours
